reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure of the model involves maximizing a likelihood function over match outcomes, where each match k is indexed by home team i(k) and away team j(k). Under idealized conditions (ρ = 0), Maher (1982) derived a linear system of equations for estimating team strengths. However, due to complexity and high dimensionality, direct numerical maximization of the full likelihood (equation 4.3) is preferred. The inclusion of teams from multiple divisions introduces inter-dependencies that require careful calibration of attack and defense parameters (α and β) across divisions. These parameters must reflect relative quality differences between divisions, which is ensured by including inter-divisional match data—such as those from cup games or promoted/relegated teams. The near orthogonality of parameter combinations simplifies optimization despite high dimensionality. The resulting model allows for probabilistic inference on match outcomes involving teams from different divisions, enabling GSI to compute posterior probabilities and GSE to simulate transitions between game states based on calibrated team attributes.
